blocks.prompt: 10. The 3rd term of a G.P. is the square of 1st term. If the 2nd term is 9 then find the 6th term.
blocks.explanation:
Sawal ke do jumle hain, aur har jumla ek equation ban jata hai.
Diya kya hai? Teesra term pehle term ka square hai, aur doosra term 9 hai.
Find kya karna hai? 6th term \(a_6 = a_1 r^5\).
Plan: pehli sharait se \(a_1 = r^2\) milega; usay doosri sharait mein rakh kar \(r^3 = 9\). Phir indices ke qawaneen se \(a_6\).
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_3 = a_1^2\), \(a_2 = 9\).
Humein find karna hai: \(a_6\).
Tareeqa: \(a_2\) aur \(a_3\) ko \(a_n = a_1 r^{n-1}\) se likh kar do equations banayenge, aur un se \(a_1\) aur \(r\) nikalenge. Lafzon ko equation mein badalna is sawal ka asal hunar hai.

Jumlon ko equations banayein
\[a_1 r^2 = a_1^2 \quad (1)\]
\[a_1 r = 9 \quad (2)\]
Kyun: "Teesra term pehle ka square hai" yani \(a_3 = a_1^2\), aur \(a_3 = a_1 r^2\). "Doosra term 9 hai" yani \(a_1 r = 9\).

(1) ko saada karein
\[r^2 = a_1 \quad (3)\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(a_1\) se divide kiya. Yeh jaaiz hai kyunke \(a_1\) zero nahi ho sakta: agar \(a_1 = 0\) hota to har term zero hota, lekin doosra term 9 hai.
Dhyan dein: Kisi cheez se divide karne se pehle hamesha check kijiye ke woh zero to nahi.

\(r\) nikalein
\[r^2 \cdot r = 9\]
\[r^3 = 9 \Rightarrow r = \sqrt[3]{9}\]
Kyun: (3) se \(a_1 = r^2\) ko (2) mein rakha: \(r^2 \cdot r = r^3\). Ab \(r\) woh number hai jise teen dafa multiply karein to 9 aaye, yani 9 ka cube root. 9 perfect cube nahi, is liye \(\sqrt[3]{9}\) hi chhor dete hain. Real number ka real cube root sirf ek hota hai.

Tasdeeq
\[a_1 = r^2 = 9^{2/3},\ a_2 = r^3 = 9\ \checkmark\]
\[a_3 = r^4 = (r^2)^2 = a_1^2\ \checkmark\]
Kyun: Doosra term waqai 9 hai, aur teesra term \(r^4\) pehle term \(r^2\) ka square hai. Dono sharait poori, is liye jawab sahi hai.
